note: Historical event template data. Sources resolve against scenario sources[].

events.title: The invasion begins
events.body: On Sunday 22 June 1941 more than 3.8 million Axis troops attack along a 2,900 km front after a massive ground and air assault; Soviet forces are largely caught unprepared (R01). Exact hour of the first attacks is not retrieved.

events.title: The Western Front air force is destroyed on the ground
events.body: In the opening hours the Luftwaffe destroys the Western Front air force on the ground and, with Abwehr-supported fifth columns, paralyses its communications; the 4th Army headquarters is cut off (R01, R04).

events.title: Brest Fortress
events.body: The 45th Infantry Division attacks the fortress after a 29-minute bombardment; about 9,000 defenders hold out; by 24 June 4,000-5,000 Soviet soldiers are captured and fighting continues to about 30 June (R10).

events.title: Tank battle at Brody-Dubno-Lutsk
events.body: From 23 to 30 June the 1st Panzer Group fights five Soviet mechanised corps in the Dubno-Lutsk-Brody triangle (R11).

events.title: Battle of Raseiniai
events.body: The 4th Panzer Group fights the Soviet 3rd and 12th Mechanised Corps near Raseiniai from 23 to 27 June, destroying most of the Northwestern Front armour (R16).

events.title: Counterstrike toward Grodno
events.body: On 24-25 June the 6th and 11th Mechanised Corps and the 6th Cavalry Corps counter-attack toward Grodno on Pavlov order and fail (R01).

events.title: Panzer groups meet east of Minsk
events.body: The 2nd and 3rd Panzer Groups meet near Minsk on 27 June and take the city the next day, closing two pockets around Bialystok and west of Minsk (R04).

events.title: Minsk falls
events.body: Minsk is captured on 28 June (R04).

events.title: Luga defence line begun
events.body: Construction of the Luga defence fortifications begins on 29 June together with the evacuation of children and women (R09).

events.title: Pavlov relieved
events.body: Stalin relieves Pavlov on 30 June; he is tried and executed on 22 July; the Western Front is destroyed in about 18 days (R01, R04).

events.title: Early July rainstorms slow the panzers
events.body: On 2 July and through the next six days a rainstorm typical of Belarusian summers slows Army Group Centre panzers while Soviet defences stiffen (R01). Army Group North attacks the Stalin Line on 2 July with the 4th Panzer Group, and Army Group South is joined by the 11th Army and Romanian forces (R01).
events.effectsNote: Restates R01: a rainstorm from 2 July for six days (hours 144) slows the Army Group Centre panzers.

events.title: Soviet mechanised counter-attack near Lepiel
events.body: On 6 July the Soviet 5th and 7th Mechanised Corps (20th Army) counter-attack the German 7th Panzer Division and are virtually wiped out (R05); R01 gives the force as the V and VII Mechanised Corps in a five-day battle with 832 of about 2,000 tanks lost, a discrepancy kept open.

events.title: Pskov reached (8 July per R01)
events.body: R01 gives 8 July for the capture of Pskov by the 4th Panzer Group; R09 gives 10 July for the capture of Ostrov and Pskov. Both dates are kept; this event uses the earlier one.

events.title: Smolensk battle begins
events.body: On 10 July the 2nd Panzer Group crosses the Dnieper; by 13 July it passes Mogilev and the 29th Motorised Division is within 18 km of Smolensk (R05).

events.title: Battle of Uman begins
events.body: From 15 July Army Group South moves to encircle the Soviet 6th and 12th Armies near Uman (R06).

events.title: German logistics strain
events.body: Four weeks into the campaign Bock concludes that difficulties are due to logistics; operations are slowed for resupply; by 2 August all three army groups have 179,500 casualties and 47,000 replacements (R01). The date within July is approximate.

events.title: Smolensk encirclement ends
events.body: The encirclement battle near Smolensk ends on 5 August; Bock reports 309,000 prisoners (R05).

events.title: Uman pocket destroyed
events.body: The Soviet 6th and 12th Armies are annihilated by 8 August (R06).

events.title: Novgorod reached
events.body: The 4th Panzer Group reaches Novgorod by 16 August and Leeb takes Kingisepp and Narva on 17 August (R09); by the end of August it is within 48 km of Leningrad (R01).

events.title: Leningrad cut off by land
events.body: On 7 September the German 20th Motorised Division seizes Shlisselburg; the road to the city is severed on 8 September (R09).

events.title: Kiev encirclement closed
events.body: Half of Army Group Centre swings south behind Kiev while Army Group South moves north; the encirclement is achieved on 16 September and Kiev is captured on 19 September (R01); the battle ends 26 September with 452,700 trapped (R07).

events.title: Operation Typhoon begins
events.body: Operation Typhoon, the German drive on Moscow, begins on 30 September (R01).
